quizName: DMV Practice Test #5 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Which lane position helps prevent other vehicles from sharing your lane?

options.text: The left portion of the lane
The center portion of the lane
The right portion of the lane

questions.correctAnswerText: The center portion of the lane
questions.explanation: Riding in the center of your lane discourages other drivers from trying to squeeze in next to you. When following another car, riding in the center also makes you more visible in their rearview mirror.

questions.question: You should increase your following distance when:

options.text: You believe stopping will be routine.

questions.explanation: You need more space to stop if the pavement is slippery, if you cannot see ahead clearly, or if traffic is heavy. Leave extra distance between you and the vehicle in front of you.

questions.question: Footrests:

options.text: May be shared by the driver and passenger
Are required for the driver and passenger

questions.correctAnswerText: Are required for the driver and passenger
questions.explanation: Both the driver and passenger must have footrests. Keep your feet firmly on the footrests for balance. This prevents your passenger from falling off and taking you with them.

questions.question: When looking through a turn, you should:

options.text: Turn just your head, not your shoulders.
Turn your head and shoulders to improve your view.
Turn your shoulders, but not your head.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn just your head, not your shoulders.
questions.explanation: When turning, look through the turn to see where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders, and keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: It is illegal to operate a motorcycle with a blood alcohol content (BAC) of:
questions.explanation: In California, drivers 21 and older cannot operate a motorcycle with a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher. Drivers under 21 cannot operate a motorcycle with a BAC of 0.01 percent or higher. Operating a motorcycle can be unsafe even below the legal limit.

questions.question: Where is the greatest risk of conflict between you and other vehicles?
questions.explanation: Intersections are where motorcycles face the greatest danger from other vehicles. The biggest risk is from oncoming cars turning left in front of motorcyclists.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Use your mirrors and look over your shoulder.
Use your mirrors. You do not need to look over your shoulder unless you notice something unusual.
Either use your mirrors or look over your shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your mirrors and look over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors and look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move. Make sure no other drivers are in your path.

questions.question: If you are being passed, you should:

options.text: Ride in the left portion of the lane.
Ride in the center portion of the lane.
Ride in the right portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: When being passed, stay in the center of the lane. Riding on either side increases the risk of collision. Riding too far to the side may also make the other driver return to your lane too soon.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions. This sign warns of a divided roadway ahead.

questions.question: When stopping, you should:
questions.explanation: Use both brakes every time you slow or stop. Using both brakes allows you to stop quickly when needed.

questions.question: Which of the following will NOT help reduce your chances of a crash?

options.text: Turn off your headlights during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off your headlights during the day.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, stay visible to other drivers. Use your signals, brake light, and correct lane position. Keep space around your motorcycle and always look ahead, behind, and to the sides.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. They tell you about road conditions ahead. This sign warns that a railroad crossing is coming.

questions.question: After riding over an object on the road, you should:

options.text: Keep riding since the danger is over.
Pull over and check your tires and rims for damage.
Stop and remove the object from the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over and check your tires and rims for damage.
questions.explanation: After hitting an object, pull off the road right away. Check your tires and rims for damage. Also check that nothing is stuck in the chain or belt before you continue.

questions.question: A pre-ride inspection:

options.text: Should only be done by a certified mechanic.

questions.explanation: Check your motorcycle before every ride. This quick inspection takes only a few minutes.

questions.question: A solid white line on the side of the road indicates:

options.text: The right edge of a traffic lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right edge of a traffic lane.
questions.explanation: A solid white line on the side of the road marks the right edge of a traffic lane.

questions.question: A motorcycle's brake light is _________ a car's brake light.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle's brake light is usually not as noticeable as a car's brake light. Other drivers may not see your brake light, especially when your taillight is on. Stay aware of this.

questions.question: When riding, jackets and pants should:

options.text: Fit loosely so wind can catch the fabric.
Fit snugly so they don't flap in the wind.
Fit tightly so you cannot move freely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fit snugly so they don't flap in the wind.
questions.explanation: Jackets and pants should fit snugly to prevent flapping. They should still be loose enough to let you move freely.

questions.question: Your lane position should:

options.text: Help you blend in with traffic.
Allow others to share your lane.

questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see and be seen. It helps you avoid wind from other vehicles, blind spots, and road hazards. It should discourage other drivers from sharing your lane and give you a way out if danger appears.

questions.question: You should inspect your motorcycle:
questions.explanation: Always inspect your motorcycle before you ride. Small problems on a motorcycle are more dangerous than on a car.

questions.question: What does a flashing red traffic light mean?

options.text: Stop completely, then go when it is safe.
Slow down and yield to other traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, then go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. Stop completely. Yield to all crossing traffic and pedestrians. Then go when it is safe.

questions.question: What is improper braking?

options.text: Should not be a concern because motorcycles have two brakes.

questions.explanation: Improper braking causes many motorcycle crashes. Learning to brake correctly is a key part of safe riding.

questions.question: If your rear wheel locks up while stopping on good pavement, what should you do?

options.text: Keep the wheel locked until you stop completely.
Release the rear brake and use only the front brake.
Release the rear brake and quickly apply it again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the wheel locked until you stop completely.
questions.explanation: If your rear wheel locks while stopping on good pavement, keep it locked until you stop. You can control your motorcycle even with a locked rear wheel if the motorcycle is upright and moving straight.

questions.question: What type of boots or shoes should a rider wear?
questions.explanation: Wear sturdy footwear that covers and supports your ankles. The soles should be hard, durable, and slip-resistant.

questions.question: What does a solid yellow traffic light mean?

options.text: The light is about to turn red.
The light is about to turn green.
Stop and wait for traffic to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: The light is about to turn red.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow light warns you that the signal is about to turn red. Slow down and stop before entering the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are already in the intersection when it turns yellow, continue through.

questions.question: Smaller vehicles like motorcycles appear to be ________ and slower than they really are.
questions.explanation: It is hard to judge how fast and how far away a small vehicle is. Do not assume that drivers of larger vehicles can accurately see your speed and location.
